roll_definition: The 30->60 roll rate is the share of installments in DPD bucket '1-30' whose NEXT installment on the same loan (ordered by NUM_INSTALMENT_NUMBER, latest NUM_INSTALMENT_VERSION per number) lands in DPD bucket '31-60' or worse ('31-60', '61-90' or '90+'). Installments with no next installment (the last one observed on a loan) are excluded from the denominator.

installments.name: Installment record
installments.text: One scheduled installment: a unique (SK_ID_PREV, NUM_INSTALMENT_VERSION, NUM_INSTALMENT_NUMBER). Payment rows are collapsed: scheduled = MAX(AMT_INSTALMENT), taken once; paid = SUM(AMT_PAYMENT).

dpd.name: DPD (days past due)
dpd.text: GREATEST(last payment day - due day, 0). The last payment is when the installment was fully settled. Installments with no payment at all are aged to day 0, the observation point.

on_time.name: On-time %
on_time.text: Installments with DPD = 0 AND paid >= 99% of the scheduled amount, divided by all installments.

coverage.name: Coverage %
coverage.text: Sum of amounts paid / sum of amounts scheduled. Can exceed 100% because borrowers prepay.

partial.name: Partial %
partial.text: Installments where 0 < paid / scheduled < 99%, divided by all installments.

late.name: Late %
late.text: Installments with DPD > 0, divided by all installments.

dpd_buckets.name: DPD buckets
dpd_buckets.text: 0, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90 and 90+ days past due. Shares by count of installments or weighted by scheduled amount.

roll_30_60.name: 30->60 roll rate
roll_30_60.text: The 30->60 roll rate is the share of installments in DPD bucket '1-30' whose NEXT installment on the same loan (ordered by NUM_INSTALMENT_NUMBER, latest NUM_INSTALMENT_VERSION per number) lands in DPD bucket '31-60' or worse ('31-60', '61-90' or '90+'). Installments with no next installment (the last one observed on a loan) are excluded from the denominator.

cure_rate.name: Cure rate
cure_rate.text: Of installments in '1-30' with a next installment, the share whose next installment is on time (DPD 0).

repeat_delinquent.name: Repeat-delinquent
repeat_delinquent.text: The borrower had at least N late installments (DPD > 0, on any of their loans) due strictly BEFORE the current installment's due day. Headline N = 2. The window frame ends at 1 PRECEDING, so there is no look-ahead.

never_late.name: Never late
never_late.text: The borrower had no late installment due before the current one.

severe_history.name: Severe history (sensitivity)
severe_history.text: The borrower had at least N installments more than 30 days late due before the current one. Same leakage-safe window. Reported separately from the headline.

outstanding.name: Outstanding (proxy)
outstanding.text: Active loans only (DAYS_TERMINATION = 365243): remaining installments x annuity. The dataset has no balance snapshots, so this is a proxy.

expected_roll.name: Expected roll amount
expected_roll.text: Repeat-delinquent 30->60 roll rate of the segment x outstanding held by its repeat-delinquent borrowers today. Used to rank early-warning segments.

ci.name: 95% confidence interval
ci.text: p +/- 1.96 * sqrt(p(1-p)/n): the range that would contain the true rate in 95% of repeated samples.

ztest.name: Two-proportion z-test
ztest.text: z = (p1 - p2) / sqrt(p_pool(1 - p_pool)(1/n1 + 1/n2)). |z| > 1.96 means the gap is significant at 5%.

sql_leakage_window:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE repeat_sequence AS
SELECT r.*,
       COALESCE(SUM(is_late::INT) OVER prior_history, 0)    AS prior_late_cnt,
       COALESCE(SUM((dpd > 30)::INT) OVER prior_history, 0) AS prior_severe_cnt
FROM roll_sequence r
WINDOW prior_history AS (
    PARTITION BY SK_ID_CURR
    ORDER BY due_day
    RANGE BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING   -- strictly earlier due days only
);
sql_fact_grain:
WITH installment AS (
    -- Collapse payment rows to the installment grain.
    SELECT SK_ID_PREV,
           NUM_INSTALMENT_VERSION,
           NUM_INSTALMENT_NUMBER,
           MAX(SK_ID_CURR)               AS SK_ID_CURR,      -- constant per loan
           MAX(DAYS_INSTALMENT)          AS due_day,         -- constant per installment
           MAX(AMT_INSTALMENT)           AS scheduled_amt,   -- constant per installment: take once
           COALESCE(SUM(AMT_PAYMENT), 0) AS paid_amt,        -- payments add up
           COUNT(AMT_PAYMENT)            AS payment_rows,
           MIN(DAYS_ENTRY_PAYMENT)       AS first_pay_day,
           MAX(DAYS_ENTRY_PAYMENT)       AS last_pay_day
    FROM stg_installments
    GROUP BY SK_ID_PREV, NUM_INSTALMENT_VERSION, NUM_INSTALMENT_NUMBER
)
